entries.solution: Implement durable reminder evaluation from C4 task state and F1 personal preferences. For a dated time schedule one hour before; for a date-only task schedule 07:00 in the company timezone; for overdue work send one current daily summary at 07:00; undated tasks remain only in Co teraz. The coordinator receives the reminder, while unassigned tasks target all bosses. A newly created or assigned task whose reminder time passed gets one prompt as soon as quiet hours permit, without replaying every missed alert. Store snooze per user/task until a chosen instant. Due-date or coordinator changes clear prior snoozes and recompute semantic intents; completion or cancellation removes future reminders. Keep date-only 07:00 as delivery metadata, never as an invented task time.
acceptance: Reminder, conversation mute, quiet hours, and per-task snooze remain independent personal controls.
Changing date or coordinator invalidates obsolete intents and snoozes; the former coordinator receives no later reminder.
Completed/cancelled tasks produce no future reminder, while reading their source alone changes nothing.
Date-only overdue status begins after that company-local day and first daily overdue summary is next day at 07:00.
tests: Deterministic clock tests cover timed/date-only/undated/overdue work, DST, create-after-07:00, reassignment, unassignment, snooze expiry, quiet hours, completion, and cancellation.
Race tests change assignee or state while a reminder is due and prove the final recipient/state is rechecked before F2 delivery.
Integration test boss-created own task still creates a reminder.
nonGoals: Editing shared task due dates from snooze, checklist-item reminders, or final Co teraz design.
Web Push transport, owned by F3.
integration: Consume C4 current task/event contracts and F1 preferences; emit typed reminder intents through F2 and task/reminder projections for H2.
Own convex/attention/reminders/** only; cross-feature composition remains a later J ticket.

entries.title: [G1] Implement optional Calendar authorization and connection lifecycle
entries.problem: Google Calendar is an optional personal integration, independent from Kiero sign-in. A boss logging in by email code may connect a different Google address, and disconnecting Calendar must never alter identity or membership. OAuth state, tokens, account switches, revoked grants, and deleted dedicated calendars need an explicit lifecycle before projection logic can be safe.
entries.solution: Implement one Google Calendar connection per user/company with server-owned OAuth state, least required scopes, encrypted credentials, and checked callback correlation. Keep Google identity distinct from B1/B2 login methods. On first confirmed connection create or recover a dedicated calendar named for the company; never create another calendar while creation/existence outcome is unknown. Store connection state, Google account identity, dedicated calendar ID, consent/scopes, last successful contact, and reconnect/cleanup status. Disconnect stops future publishing immediately and attempts to remove Kiero-managed copies while preserving the calendar and user-created events. Membership loss follows the same stop/cleanup path. A Polish unstyled entry point exposes connect, reconnect, switch account, and explicit recreate-after-confirmed-deletion operations.
acceptance: Email-code and Google-login users can connect a different Google account without linking or changing Kiero identity.
OAuth callbacks are bound to initiating user/company and reject replay, wrong company, missing scopes, and revoked membership.
Unknown create/read outcomes never cause blind duplicate calendar creation; confirmed deletion offers explicit Odtwórz.
Disconnect or membership loss stops new company data immediately and records unconfirmed cleanup for the user.
tests: Use two real Google accounts in isolated development/staging to connect, revoke consent, reconnect after more than a week, switch account, delete the calendar, and disconnect.
Failure injection covers callback replay, state mismatch, token refresh failure, timeout after calendar creation, ambiguous 404, and cleanup without Google permission.
Verify Calendar disconnect leaves every Kiero login method and session usable.
nonGoals: Importing private calendars, Google Tasks, two-way Kiero edits, or paid/production OAuth rollout.
Event eligibility and field mapping, owned by G2.
integration: Consume B3 current user/company authority and I1 environment bindings; export typed connection state and credential capability to G2/G3/G4.
Own only connection/OAuth paths. Register the barebones screen via A4 without changing shared app composition.

entries.title: [G2] Implement deterministic Calendar projection and personal scope
entries.problem: Kiero must project its current plan to each boss's dedicated Google calendar without turning Google into authority. Eligibility is personal: selected projects, coordinator assignment, unassigned tasks, personal hides, and retained obligations in closed projects all matter. Date-only values, true intervals, and hour-without-duration values require deterministic mapping.
entries.solution: Build a pure, typed projection module plus Convex projection state. Select planned events and open tasks (Do zrobienia, W toku, Czeka) coordinated by the connected boss or unassigned, filtered by that boss's selected projects. Include past unresolved obligations and all known future dates; exclude proposals, approximate values, and unresolved conflicts. Map a date to all-day, a known start/end to an interval, and a lone time to a five-minute Google marker whose title/description says it is a time marker, never a five-minute duration fact. Preserve Europe/Warsaw semantics and describe company time. Generate short Polish titles, project, state/meaning, relevant location, and an authenticated Kiero link; exclude conversations, media, and financial notes. Maintain personal hide and selected-project state independently from notification preferences.
acceptance: Each qualifying Kiero task/event has one stable projection identity per user/company and Google account; task and related event stay separate.
Kiero owns title, date/time, and description while remembered personal color, reminders, and free/busy survive managed updates.
User deletion/move becomes a personal hide that survives corrections, reopen, requalification, and reconnect until explicit restore.
Completion/cancellation or unresolved/removed date withdraws the copy; elapsed time or project closure alone does not.
tests: Table-driven domain tests cover all-day, interval, five-minute marker, DST transitions, past unresolved work, coordinator changes, unassigned tasks, selected projects, closed projects, and separate task/event identities.
Property tests prove deterministic semantic IDs and no private source/media/financial content in payloads.
Integration fixtures preserve personal settings and distinguish Kiero deletion from user hide.
nonGoals: Calling Google APIs, OAuth lifecycle, Calendar UI, or importing changes into Kiero.
Final calendar information architecture or visual design.
integration: Consume C4 canonical task/event/date contracts and G1 connection identity; export desired projection records and diff inputs to G3 plus settings projections to G4/I3.
Own packages/domain/calendar/** and convex/calendar/projection/**; do not edit C4 records or global composition.

entries.title: [G3] Reconcile Calendar writes, unknown outcomes and reconnects
entries.problem: Google writes happen outside Convex transactions. A timeout may follow a successful create, change signals may be lost, copies may be manually edited/deleted/moved, and stale jobs can arrive after a newer Kiero correction. Blind retry can duplicate calendars or events and delayed work can republish superseded facts.
entries.solution: Implement durable reconciliation from G2 desired state to the dedicated calendar supplied by G1. Store semantic identity, remote ID, desired revision, observed fields, attempt/outcome state, and whether deletion was Kiero-owned or a detected personal hide. Use idempotent create/update/delete logic, bounded retry, and read-after-unknown reconciliation. Recheck connection, membership, desired revision, scope, and hide state before each external call and before accepting its result. Restore Kiero-owned fields after manual Google edits while preserving captured personal settings. Treat move outside the dedicated calendar as hide. On reconnect, recover the same calendar when possible and reconcile current state; after confirmed calendar deletion wait for explicit recreate. Measure save-to-Google acceptance and expose last success, pending, failed, reconnect-needed, and possible-cleanup-remains states.
acceptance: Retries and concurrent changes converge to current G2 projections without duplicate managed events or calendars.
Unknown create/update/delete outcomes remain explicit until reconciled and never become assumed success or blind recreation.
A stale job cannot overwrite a newer due date, restore an ineligible item, or publish after disconnect/membership revocation.
The system records enough timing to evaluate the 95% within 60 seconds target without claiming it before J4.
tests: Real Google integration tests use two accounts for edits, deletes, moves, hide/restore, completion/reopen, account reconnect after more than a week, and project/assignee changes.
Fault tests inject timeout after remote success, 404 ambiguity, stale revision, lost change signal, token expiry, parallel retries, and revoked membership.
Prove reconnect converges without duplicates and does not replay superseded Kiero state.
nonGoals: Two-way mutation of Kiero facts, copying private calendars, or guaranteeing Google availability.
Final settings UI, owned by G4.
integration: Consume G1 credential/connection capability, G2 desired projections, A3 durable executor, and B3 live access; export status/diagnostics to G4, H4, I2, I4, and I6.
Own convex/calendar/sync/**. Cross-feature end-to-end wiring waits for J1/J2/J5.

Consume membership/connection revocation to stop new transfer and attempt managed-copy cleanup only while Google authorization permits. Preserve unknown/leftover status without retaining Kiero access.

entries.title: [G4] Expose unstyled Calendar settings and sync diagnostics
entries.problem: Bosses need to operate and diagnose the optional Calendar integration without reading logs or confusing it with Kiero sign-in. The application must expose personal project scope, hidden-copy recovery, pending/failed sync, reconnection, and explicit calendar recreation in a usable Polish barebones screen.
entries.solution: Build an unstyled responsive Calendar settings feature using only G1-G3 typed queries and commands. Show connected Google account, dedicated calendar, selected projects, last successful synchronization, pending count, actionable error/reconnect state, and unconfirmed cleanup residue. Allow connect/reconnect/disconnect, account switch, project selection, restore of personally hidden copies, and explicit Odtwórz only after G1 confirms calendar deletion. Explain that Kiero remains authoritative, synchronization is one-way, Google reminders/personal fields may remain personal, and disconnect does not affect login. Link a managed event back to the current Kiero task/event route. Keep controls keyboard accessible and Polish; use simple semantic HTML and existing A4 shell, with no final component library or styling system.
acceptance: Every state in G1/G3 has a distinct Polish status and a next action where recovery is possible.
Project scope and hidden items are personal and editable without changing company facts or notification mutes.
The UI cannot offer blind recreate for unknown existence, cannot imply two-way sync, and cannot show success while work is pending/failed.
Mobile and desktop flows remain functional with keyboard/screen-reader labels despite barebones presentation.
tests: Component/integration tests exercise disconnected, connecting, healthy, pending, partial failure, reconnect-needed, confirmed deleted, unknown, hidden-copy, and cleanup-residue states.
Browser test against development services performs connect, project toggle, hide restore, disconnect, and deep link from a Calendar fixture.
Failure test proves stale UI commands are rejected when membership or connection revision changed.
nonGoals: Final UX/UI, design tokens, Calendar provider logic, or editing Kiero dates from Google.
Qualifying the week-long/two-account contract, owned by J4.
integration: Consume G1-G3 feature exports and A4 host registration. Expose stable route/action contracts for future UX replacement without requiring domain rewrites.
Own apps/web/src/features/calendar/** only. A narrow feature registration may touch A4's registry; shared full composition remains J work.

entries.title: [H1] Expose conversation, project memory and source correction flows
entries.problem: The backend source and memory contracts need a real usable surface before final UX design. Bosses must see one company conversation, switch project context, inspect source-backed findings, answer clarifications, and correct prior information without editing immutable messages or hiding provenance.
entries.solution: Implement Polish, unstyled conversation and memory routes in the A4 host. Render paged D1 logical sources once in company order with project associations, actual author, processing state, agent questions/answers, and links to retained evidence. Project filters show fragments that still point to the same source ID. Show C2 current findings with known/unknown/conflicted/not-applicable state, revisions, provenance, and update status. A source correction is a new reply/message referencing the old source; a direct structured-field correction uses C2's separate audited command. Clear updates may be applied autonomously, while ambiguous contradictions display E3's sourced clarification and block affected automation. Integrate F1 read operations but keep visual treatment deliberately simple and replaceable.
acceptance: One mixed source appears consistently in company and project views with a single source URL, actual author, and no divergent editable copies.
Users can submit a new correcting source, answer a clarification, and inspect old/current revisions and provenance.
Conflicted or updating findings are visibly distinct and cannot be presented as settled facts.
All routes enforce B3 access through backend operations; Polish UI works on narrow mobile and desktop without final styling.
Consume the already-proved J1 commands. Replace its minimal capture/read controls through the declared feature entry without duplicating backend state or making a second conversation store.
tests: Browser integration covers company feed, project filter, mixed source, agent question/reply, correction, concurrent revision conflict, unread transition, and revoked membership.
Use real Convex fixtures and E3 outputs; verify pagination and reactive updates rather than local mock state.
Failure fixtures show accepted-but-processing, partial media analysis, failed analysis, stale correction, and missing evidence without losing the source.
nonGoals: Final bubbles, typography, design system, voice capture, search, or direct database repair.
Inventing memory rules outside C2/E3 contracts.
integration: Consume A4 shell, C1/C2 queries and commands, D1 source projections, E3 plans/questions, and F1 read API; export stable routes/deep links to F3, G2/G4, and future UX work.
Own conversation/memory feature paths; use A4/A2 exports and build on J1 and defer full joins to J2/J5.

entries.title: [H2] Expose tasks, events, extensions and Co teraz
entries.problem: Tasks, events, typed extensions, and Co teraz must be exercised against the real domain model before final UX work. The surface must preserve non-obvious rules: a parent task completes independently from checklist items, elapsed time does not complete an event, and closed projects can retain open obligations.
entries.solution: Build unstyled Polish routes for project work, typed extension fields, and a per-user Co teraz list. Use C4 commands for task states Do zrobienia, W toku, Czeka, Wykonane, Anulowane and event states Planowane, Odbyło się, Anulowane. Display one-level checklists inside tasks but require an explicit parent state change; checklist completion never derives parent completion. Keep coordinator membership separate from external executor contact. Support exact/date-only/unknown dates and display unknown money tax basis without guessing. Render C3 extension definitions by supported primitive/object/list types and stable field IDs. Co teraz includes assigned and unassigned open work, questions needing response, and remaining obligations from closed projects, with current F4 reminder/snooze state.
acceptance: Bosses can create/update tasks, checklists, events, coordinator/executor, dates, states, and supported extension values through checked commands.
Completing every checklist item leaves the parent unchanged; completing/cancelling the parent is explicit.
A past planned event stays Planowane until explicitly marked Odbyło się or Anulowane.
Co teraz exposes actionable work and questions across active/closed projects and links to authoritative records.
tests: Browser integration uses real C3/C4/F4 data for create/edit/state transitions, checklist independence, closed-project obligation, overdue date-only work, snooze, reassignment, and unassigned work.
Failure tests cover stale revisions, revoked membership, invalid extension version/value, removed coordinator, and concurrent checklist/parent changes.
Accessibility smoke verifies forms and state labels in Polish on mobile and desktop widths.
nonGoals: Final task/calendar UX, nested checklist trees, derived parent completion, or Google Calendar synchronization.
Creating new domain primitives outside C3/C4.
integration: Consume A4, C3, C4, and F4 exports; expose record routes consumed by F3 notification clicks, G2 links, H3 search, and future UX integration.
Own work/extensions/now feature paths. Keep shared full composition changes for J1/J2/J5.

entries.title: [H3] Expose search, media anchors and source history
entries.problem: Users need to find evidence across authored text, speech transcripts, image OCR, current findings, and history, then inspect the exact retained representation and correction chain. Search results that omit tenant checks, hydrate stale revisions, or point at obsolete media coordinates would undermine the source-backed memory contract.
entries.solution: Implement unstyled Polish search and source-detail routes over E5 retrieval, D3 authorized media access, C2 revisions, and C5 withdrawal/recomputation state. Search text/transcript/OCR with project, author, and date filters; label semantic/full-text coverage and disclose degraded semantic retrieval rather than interpreting no hit as no fact. Hydrate every result against current company access, source state, and index generation. Source detail shows immutable authored content, all retained representations, transcript/OCR segments and time/coordinate anchors, project fragments, findings/provenance, corrections, withdrawals, and dependent recomputation status. Audio playback uses authenticated range streaming; image highlights resolve against the actual retained normalized/original-exception representation. Paginate history rather than loading one growing object.
acceptance: Search finds representative Polish text, transcript, and OCR evidence with filters and opens the authoritative source/revision.
Withdrawn/deleted/revised evidence cannot appear as current through a stale vector result; degraded retrieval is visible.
Media anchors resolve to D3's current retained representation and require live access for every request/range.
History and correction dependencies are inspectable in Polish barebones UI on mobile and desktop.
Expose source withdrawal and reassignment controls through C5, with impact/history and the original source identity/read state preserved. Do not represent withdrawal as permanent deletion.

Recheck current company access for source metadata, transcript/OCR, revisions and history as well as media. Revocation while source detail is open must discard protected subscriptions/views and deny fresh reads.
tests: Real integration fixtures cover text, long-audio segments, normalized-image OCR coordinates, revised finding, withdrawn source, index generation cutover, and company isolation.
Failure tests revoke membership during playback, delete/replace a representation, return a stale vector ID, fail embeddings, and interrupt pagination.
Browser tests verify filters, deep links, range seek, evidence highlight, correction history, and recomputation status.
nonGoals: Final search relevance tuning or visual design, editing sources, public media URLs, or building E5 indexes.
Cross-feature polished navigation beyond stable routes.
integration: Consume A4, E5 retrieval results, D3 streams, C2 revisions, and C5 dependency state; export stable source URLs used by H1, E6 answers, exports, and future UX.
Own search/source-detail feature paths and register narrowly via A4; defer complete composition to J tickets.

entries.title: [H4] Expose audited processing inspection and GM retry controls
entries.problem: During alpha, explicit GM access must make failed processing diagnosable and recoverable without silent impersonation, immutable-source edits, arbitrary database repair, or contamination of boss read and success metrics. Retry and deliberate reanalysis also have different provenance and version semantics.
entries.solution: Implement an audited GM processing inspector and checked operations API. Require B4's explicit GM mode and current alpha-company scope for every query/command. Show protected source/run detail, stage states, attempts, approved model route, pipeline/prompt/schema versions, redacted provider diagnostics, derived changes, and current blockers. Allow retry only for a failed/stuck compatible stage and preserve semantic run identity; allow deliberate reanalysis as a new linked run using the server-approved E3/E2 configuration. Record real GM actor, reason, command, target revision, result, and timestamps in canonical audit records. UI is Polish, visibly identifies GM mode, and does not mark sources read or increment autonomous alpha metrics.
acceptance: Ordinary members cannot open or invoke GM operations, and GM scope ends when alpha access is revoked.
Retry resumes approved compatible work without editing the source; reanalysis creates a linked run and cannot select an arbitrary model.
Every inspection-changing action is attributable to the GM and preserves boss authorship/read state/activity metrics.
Stale revision, already-running stage, and unsupported workflow version are rejected with actionable Polish messages.

The initial panel consumes generic canonical stage/attempt/audit records plus I2 redacted diagnostics. J2 later registers all media/retrieval stages; H4 does not falsely claim those unimplemented executors work.
tests: Integration tests use real B4 authority and E3 processing records for inspect, failed-stage retry, duplicate retry, linked reanalysis, completion race, and revoked GM/company access.
Verify audit records are canonical, diagnostics are redacted, and immutable source bytes/text never change.
Browser smoke checks clear GM banner, reason entry, status progression, and no boss unread/usage mutation.
nonGoals: General admin SQL/database repair, model selection, source editing, production support tooling, or final GM UX.
Implementing provider routing or processing stages.
integration: Consume A4, B4 authority, E3 run contracts, A3 executor, and I2 redacted diagnostics; export retry/reanalysis audit events to I2 and recovery evidence to J2/J5.
Own GM processing and processing-operation paths. Shared application composition stays with J integration tickets.

entries.title: [I1] Verify CLI access and prepare isolated EU development resources
entries.problem: The architecture depends on real isolated Convex, Cloudflare, R2, Container, OAuth, email, push, observability, and backup capabilities, but current environment facts are incomplete. The user reports Convex CLI access, plain `convex` is not currently verified on PATH/authenticated, Wrangler exists at /opt/homebrew/bin/wrangler, and secret presence has been verified only by name. Implementation tickets need stable environment bindings without exposing credentials or accidentally creating paid production services.
entries.solution: Perform a read-first CLI/account preflight and prepare checked-in environment descriptors for local development and synthetic staging. Resolve the repository-supported Convex invocation and verify authentication/project access without printing tokens. Verify Wrangler identity/capabilities, existing account/resource visibility, required EU jurisdiction options, and feasibility of distinct media/export versus backup permissions. Confirm OPENROUTER_API_KEY is available locally and as the named GitHub secret by presence only; document how runtime bindings consume it. Define environment names, non-secret variable schema, secret-name inventory, resource naming, and evidence commands. Create only free/reversible development resources already authorized by the project; record commands for any paid, production, domain, OAuth verification, or irreversible resource as pending rather than executing it.
acceptance: A fresh agent can run one documented preflight that reports each required capability as verified, unavailable, or pending without revealing secret values.
Local, synthetic staging, and future alpha production identities/bindings cannot be confused by default commands.
Convex/Cloudflare region and plan facts are measured from actual accessible tooling where possible and unverified claims remain explicit.
No provider plan is changed and no paid or production service is created by this ticket.

A3 must have usable isolated Convex development project access and Cloudflare gateway/R2 bindings or a precise prerequisite before it can pass. Record each additional resource as reused, provisioned within already-authorized development scope, or explicitly pending; a descriptor alone is not a deployment proof.
Start from integrated A0 so this issue PR receives the configured thermo-nuclear and unslop review. Preserve its workflow, vendored skills and accepted repository instructions.
tests: Run the preflight in a clean shell and CI-safe no-secret mode; prove missing CLI, missing auth, missing binding, wrong account, and unavailable capability yield actionable failures.
Validate descriptors with a local non-secret shape check; A3 later checks them against A2 configuration schemas and check repository scans contain secret names but no values.
Capture dated CLI versions and sanitized command outputs in docs/evidence/environment.
nonGoals: Deploying the application, purchasing/upgrading plans, creating production OAuth consent, or proving workload performance.
Changing accepted providers or architecture.
integration: Produce environment binding contracts consumed by A3, D2/D5/D6, F3, G1, I2, I5, and I7; own the non-secret binding skeletons listed below; A3 consumes and validates them without a second writer.

Own infra/environments/**, docs/evidence/environment/**, apps/*/wrangler.jsonc, convex.json and infra/bindings/**; report missing prerequisites to the map owner instead of silently changing downstream scope.

After A0, this ticket owns environment discovery/descriptors independently of A2. A3 reconciles the descriptor and chosen CLI/package versions with the certified runtime contracts. Resource-owning feature tickets provision their actual development bindings as part of their real integration proof; a missing credential or resource remains blocked, not a mock pass.

entries.title: [I2] Implement redacted diagnostics, health checks and cost alerts
entries.problem: Convex Free does not provide the promised native platform-log stream. Alpha operations still need redacted application events, Cloudflare diagnostics, independent silence detection, processing/save/recovery alerts, and all-in cost visibility without leaking sources, transcripts, media, prompts, tokens, or credentials.
entries.solution: Implement a typed diagnostic event boundary in Convex/gateway code and Axiom Personal configuration for the accepted retention window. Emit allowed IDs, status, error class, latency, usage, provider route, and cost metadata from A3 workflows and gateway integrations; resolve protected content only through domain access. Treat telemetry delivery as best effort and canonical audit/domain records as authority. Configure three monitor groups: source-save plus failed/stuck processing; backup freshness/health including an external heartbeat that detects total backend silence; and aggregate costs/limits with owner-visible 400 PLN warning and 500 PLN stronger alert. Track Convex/Cloudflare/R2/Containers/Images/AI/email/observability/backup estimates and provider hard caps. Explicitly label native Convex log history unavailable on Free instead of simulating it.
acceptance: Structured diagnostics cover required operations with trace/run IDs and no source body, transcript, media, prompt, token, secret, or raw provider payload.
Three monitor groups produce useful owner notifications for save/processing, health/recovery, and cost/limit conditions.
A missing-heartbeat test detects backend silence independently of application event delivery.
Dashboards state retention and blind spots accurately; application events do not claim full native Convex logging.
tests: Trigger synthetic save failure, stuck processing, stale backup heartbeat, missing application events, and 400/500 PLN threshold crossings in isolated staging.
Snapshot/redaction tests feed adversarial source text, filenames, prompts, auth headers, URLs, and provider errors and assert no sensitive fields reach the sink.
Fault tests drop/duplicate/out-of-order telemetry and prove domain workflows remain correct.
nonGoals: Building a custom logging platform, upgrading to Convex Pro, storing content in logs, or treating telemetry as audit history.
Implementing backup/export/AI business workflows.
integration: Consume A3 runtime events and I1 bindings; export a small diagnostic API for every feature plus health/cost status used by H4, I5, I7, and J qualification.
Own telemetry/observability paths; feature tickets add event calls through the exported boundary, while J tickets verify cross-system coverage.

entries.title: [I3] Export consistent company snapshots with protected downloads
entries.problem: A company administrator needs a portable, readable export while the company remains active. Reading tables and media at different times would produce an internally inconsistent archive; static bearer downloads could survive admin revocation or permanent source deletion and expose another tenant's data.
entries.solution: Implement an asynchronous export operation anchored to one consistent company snapshot/revision. Assemble a bounded archive in the selected export worker containing a readable escaped HTML index, versioned JSON, source/finding/task/event/extension/history data, and every retained media representation referenced by that snapshot. Export the accepted shared business records, their authorship and history. Personal read/notification settings and Calendar connection/hide/cursor state are account or integration state, not part of the business archive; shared tasks/events remain included. Exclude authentication secrets, platform backups, diagnostics content, provider tokens and other tenants. Store export-source links for invalidation. Downloads use an authenticated gateway check for current company administrator rights on every request, expire 24 hours after completion, support bounded streaming, and become inaccessible immediately if a later permanent source deletion affects the archive.
acceptance: Concurrent company writes do not create mixed-revision JSON, HTML, history, or media; the archive declares its snapshot time/schema version.
HTML and archive paths safely escape hostile user content, and no record/media from another company can enter the result.
Only a current administrator can start or download an export; revocation, expiry, or linked permanent deletion invalidates access immediately.
Completed bytes are cleaned after the 24-hour window or invalidation and status remains auditable.
tests: Run a real export while continuously writing tasks/sources and compare every JSON/HTML/media reference to the declared snapshot.

Adversarial tests cover HTML/script content, path traversal filenames, huge media, missing object, cross-tenant IDs, admin transfer/revocation during assembly/download, range requests, and deletion after completion.
Verify partial archives never become downloadable and retry does not create divergent published snapshots.
nonGoals: Platform backup, public share links, import/restore, final export UX, or exporting authentication/provider secrets.
Changing source retention policy.
integration: Consume C3/C4 domain snapshots, D3 retained-media streams and B3 current admin checks; publish export-source links for I4 invalidation and diagnostics to I2.
Own export worker/backend/feature paths. Register a simple Polish status/download screen through A4; defer shared full composition to J.

entries.title: [I4] Purge deleted sources and invalidate all derived access
entries.problem: Permanent deletion must remove access immediately and prevent reconstruction through derivatives, search, notifications, Calendar, exports, retries, or later recovery. Database deletion alone is insufficient because media, indexes, remote effects, active streams, and old backup snapshots can outlive the canonical row.
entries.solution: Implement a deletion coordinator that first tombstones the logical source and revokes all application reads atomically, then enumerates provenance/dependency records and durable purge intents for active media, normalized representations, transcripts/OCR, findings/recomputations, vectors/full-text records, notification/push work, Calendar copies, and linked exports. Write a content-free deletion/revocation ledger entry outside application database rollback authority using stable opaque identities and monotonic ordering. Recheck tombstones in every worker before publishing derived output. Invalidate affected I3 archives immediately and purge active/reconstructing content within 24 hours; isolated backup bytes may survive only until reference-aware expiry within 30 days. Record external outcomes as known/unknown and reconcile without making deleted content readable.
acceptance: After the initiating operation commits, source/media/search/export access fails immediately across existing sessions and new requests.
All active and reconstructing derivatives are either verified purged within 24 hours or remain visibly failed/unknown with retry state and alerting.
The external ledger contains no user content yet can prevent resurrection after an old database restore.
Late AI, upload, push, Calendar, export, or index results cannot republish or expose the deleted source.

Expose an administrator-only unstyled impact preview and explicit permanent-delete confirmation, with pending/complete/failed external-cleanup state. This is a real registered feature, distinct from ordinary withdrawal.

Permission checks deny new reads/range requests after the committed tombstone. Bytes already delivered cannot be retracted; active-stream tests report that boundary rather than promise physical erasure of a recipient copy.
tests: End-to-end deletion races active media streaming, image/STT/AI completion, vector indexing, push delivery, Calendar write, export assembly/download, and repeated delete requests.
Fault tests lose acknowledgements and interrupt each purge stage; prove idempotent retry, unknown-outcome reconciliation, 24-hour tracking, and I2 alerts.
Restore an older fixture in quarantine and prove the external ledger suppresses deleted content before access.
nonGoals: Ordinary correction/withdrawal semantics, immediate erasure from isolated backup sets, or legal-policy claims deferred in Q195.
Deleting unrelated user-created Google events.
integration: Consume C5 dependency graph, D3 media authority, E5 search deletion, F3/G3 external intents, and I3 archive links; export ledger/reconciliation contracts to I5/I6 and diagnostics to I2.
Own deletion/purge paths. Producers integrate via typed tombstone checks; global race qualification belongs to J2/J5.

entries.title: [I5] Create complete scheduled EU backups and retention manifests
entries.problem: A database snapshot is not a complete Kiero recovery set when retained media lives in R2. Backups every 15 minutes can overlap, fail midway, exceed Free/Starter limits, or delete shared media prematurely. A green scheduler invocation must not be confused with verified recoverability.
entries.solution: Implement the separate EU backup Container and Convex-owned schedule using the pinned documented export mechanism. Every 15 minutes acquire a single-run lease, export a database snapshot, copy/verify every retained media object referenced at that snapshot, and publish an immutable manifest only after hashes/sizes and reference closure succeed. Store complete sets in a private EU R2 backup bucket with permissions isolated from media/export workers. Measure freshness from database snapshot time, not completion time, and emit I2 health/cost events before one-hour age. Retain frequent complete sets for 48 hours and daily complete sets through day 14; perform reference-aware media collection across surviving manifests. Carry I4's content-free deletion/revocation ledger separately and enforce backup-content expiry within 30 days.
acceptance: The schedule runs every 15 minutes without overlapping writers and never labels partial database/media output complete.
Each complete manifest verifies the database snapshot and all referenced retained media with EU storage and isolated credentials.
Retention keeps frequent sets for 48 hours and daily sets through day 14 without deleting media referenced by any surviving manifest.
Observed export/snapshot/storage/egress costs and Free/Starter hard limits are measured; frequency is never silently reduced to fit a plan.
tests: Run the actual accessible service plan and interrupt export, media copy, manifest publish, cleanup, and overlapping scheduler attempts; verify resumable/idempotent recovery.
Corrupt or omit an object and prove completeness fails and freshness alerting continues.
Advance retention fixtures through 48 hours, 14 days, and deleted-source 30-day expiry; verify reference-aware cleanup and sanitized evidence.
nonGoals: Opening restored data to users, application exports, changing provider plans automatically, or claiming RPO/RTO before I6 measurement.
Protecting against every account-wide provider incident.
integration: Consume A3 scheduling/runtime, D3 retained-media inventory, I1 EU bindings, I2 health/cost events, and I4 external ledger contract; export immutable recovery manifests to I6.
Own backup worker/backend/infra paths. Keep deployment/release composition in I7 and full qualification in J5.

entries.title: [I6] Prove quarantine restore with deletion and revocation replay
entries.problem: Backup creation alone does not prove the accepted one-hour recovery point and eight-hour recovery time. Restoring an old snapshot can revive deleted content, revoked sessions, stale memberships, obsolete workflow state, or uncertain Google/push effects unless recovery happens in quarantine and current external constraints are replayed before anything runs.
entries.solution: Build a recovery tool and runbook that selects a verified I5 manifest, restores database plus referenced media into an isolated quarantine environment, and keeps users, AI, schedulers, push, email, Calendar, and exports disabled. Apply I4's content-free deletion/revocation ledger in strict order; invalidate restored sessions/method changes as required by B2, purge forbidden content, reconcile retained representations, and classify unknown G3/external outcomes without replaying them blindly. Restore compatible application code, component/auth/workflow versions, configuration schema, and scheduler definitions before validation. Rebuild disposable search projections only after canonical data is safe. Emit a versioned evidence record with snapshot age, elapsed restore time, reconciled counts, unresolved items, and explicit go/no-go; opening access is a separate checked final action.
acceptance: A measured drill restores a complete set with snapshot age at most one hour and reaches validated service readiness within eight hours, or records the target as failed.
No user, worker, AI, or external integration can access/act on quarantine data before ledger replay and validation finish.
Deleted content and revoked access from after the snapshot remain deleted/revoked after restore.
Unknown Calendar/push outcomes are reconciled or safely held, never blindly replayed.
tests: Perform a real isolated drill with post-snapshot source deletion, session/membership revocation, Google unknown outcome, pending workflow, missing derived index, and scheduler configuration.
Fault injection interrupts restore, ledger replay, media reconciliation, and validation; rerun proves monotonic idempotent progress.
Negative drills use incomplete/corrupt manifests and unavailable dependencies and prove access cannot open.
nonGoals: Automatic production failover, normal release rollback via database restore, or claiming cross-provider disaster independence.
Changing retention/RPO/RTO policy.
integration: Consume I5 manifests, I4 external ledger, B2 revocation state, G3 reconciliation contracts, and A3 workflow version registry; produce evidence for J5/readiness.
Own recovery tools/evidence only. Any environment opening command must call existing checked authorities rather than patching feature data directly.

entries.title: [I7] Implement compatible release, migration and safe PWA update flows
entries.problem: Schema, workflow, gateway, and PWA releases can overlap old tabs, in-flight durable work, recordings, uploads, and local drafts. Replacing all layers atomically is unrealistic; forced reload or database rollback could lose user input or discard newer data. Production also needs an explicit human trigger after synthetic staging.
entries.solution: Implement pinned GitHub Actions checks and release workflow that deploys an isolated synthetic staging environment, records immutable versions/evidence, and exposes an explicit production trigger. Define expand-migrate-contract releases: add backward-compatible schema/API support, run resumable idempotent migrations in bounded batches with progress, release workers/client while retaining executable support for old workflow versions, then remove compatibility only after measured absence. Provide compatible code rollback/forward repair; never automate old database restoration as release rollback. In the PWA, detect a new version, persist/migrate the local draft first, and show a Polish update prompt only at a safe point. Recording, editing, and upload defer reload; unsupported old clients receive a clear update requirement while their recoverable draft remains available. Security/session revocation stays immediate regardless of client age.
acceptance: A schema expansion, resumable migration, mixed old/new clients/workers, and later support removal complete without corrupting canonical data.
Production deployment cannot happen as an implicit consequence of checks/staging and uses environment-scoped secrets.
PWA update never force-reloads during recording/edit/upload and preserves a draft across client schema migration.
Rollback/forward repair does not restore an old database or resurrect revoked access.
tests: Release rehearsal deploys expansion, interrupts/resumes migration, runs old in-flight workflow and old tab, updates the client, verifies compatibility, then removes old support.
Browser/device tests update during recording, text editing, resumable upload, offline draft, draft-schema change, and unsupported-client recovery.
CI tests wrong-environment secrets, failed staging checks, concurrent release attempt, migration retry, and immediate revocation on an old client.
nonGoals: Automatic production promotion, final update-modal design, blue-green perfection, or using backup restore for routine release recovery.
Changing accepted service plans or feature behavior.
integration: Consume A3 workflow version registry, A4 app host, D4 draft/upload states, F3 service worker/push registration, I1 bindings, and I2 release diagnostics; export release/version evidence to J4/J5.
Own release/migration/PWA-update/infra paths. Feature packages expose compatibility adapters; J tickets perform full cross-feature release qualification.

entries.title: [J1] Prove the first real text-to-memory loop in the barebones app
entries.problem: Isolated modules cannot show whether a real boss can send a source and get useful, correct current project memory.
entries.solution: Create the plain core-text feature and compose a narrow real path: authenticate two bosses in one test company, create/select a project, send text, persist one source, call the configured OpenRouter route, publish checked memory and read/correct it with source history.
acceptance: Run against real development Convex and server-owned OpenRouter, using synthetic Polish material. Show distinct sending/saved/processing/result states and actual provider/configuration metadata in protected evidence.
A mixed text source can produce company/project information while preserving one original and real author. Both bosses see the same canonical result through the app.

Send a clear correction as a new source and verify the new current value plus previous history. The early path may use direct structured queries and does not pretend semantic retrieval or all domain tools are already available.
AI failure leaves the accepted source and permits later retry. Lost response/retry does not create another source or duplicate domain mutation. Every committed change has valid provenance.
Record a repeatable smoke and immutable evidence. Missing runtime registration is fixed here or tracked as a prerequisite; a mock-only route cannot close this checkpoint.
tests: Browser plus real backend: one project, two bosses, send/read/correct and refresh/reconnect persistence.
Provider failure, duplicate submit/unknown response, newer correction against delayed old plan.
Inspect DB/current query, revision history and original source identity against independent expectations.
nonGoals: No dependency on audio, photos, Calendar, final UX or complete alpha qualification.
integration: Own the registered core-text feature and text composition using A4 plus the B/C/D/E interfaces. H1 later replaces/enriches these controls, consuming the same commands; J2 completes the full-flow join.

Prove explicit new-source correction of one current finding here. Full withdrawal/reassignment, dependent tasks, semantic retrieval and clarification tool coverage are later J2 obligations and are visibly unavailable until integrated.

entries.title: [J2] Join all capture modes, search and agent tools under failure
entries.problem: Full capture, tools and retrieval can exist separately while the application still has incomplete or divergent state transitions.
entries.solution: Join the real voice/photo/text capture, extraction, core and extension/task tools, source-backed answers, retrieval, project views, read-state operations and GM processing controls. Exercise the accepted scenarios through the barebones app and canonical persistence.
acceptance: One mixed source survives complete attachment acceptance and partial extraction; missing images/segments remain explicit and the text-only fallback never claims vision work.

Agent routing consumes typed extension/catalog and task/event operations. Retrieval hydrates current authorized revisions and enriches answers without making obsolete evidence current. Register indexing of transcript/OCR and subsequent corrections.
Clarification replies resolve the correct question and publish checked results; explicit clear corrections apply autonomously. Delayed plans cannot defeat a later correction.
Wire complete source detail/playback, source anchors/history, project aliases, work/Co teraz and personal read states. GM retry/reanalysis is audited and cannot alter boss read/activity metrics.

Task/checklist independence, closed-project obligations, firm data and source withdrawal are reachable through real controls. Record the entire twelve-scenario prototype behavior as actual backend evidence where applicable; remaining external integration proofs stay with J4.
tests: Real multimodal end-to-end flow with text, retained audio, phone image and mixed multi-project source.
Failures at extraction/planning/commit; revocation while work is queued; repeated stage delivery; source withdrawal and independent corroboration.
Browser tests for source-backed answer, clarification, direct correction, checklist and Co teraz using current persisted state.
nonGoals: No approval of final UI design, live-alpha success claim or replacement of physical device/Calendar proofs.
integration: Own final core composition entries. Explicitly connect E5 retrieval to E6 tools, E4 extraction to E5 indexing, F1 reads to conversation/source views and C5 recomputation to source correction. J3/J4/J5 consume this joined app.
Wire B3 revocation to C4 open-task successor/unassignment and F4 recalculation, D2 upload checks, B2 sessions and F1 attention state. Prove core denial without waiting for delayed cleanup.

entries.title: [J3] Qualify AI quality, fallback behavior and processing latency
entries.problem: Working model calls do not establish Polish extraction, memory correctness, fallback behavior or accepted latency.
entries.solution: Run the independently grounded corpus through the actual integrated candidate, report every modality and stage, then qualify the chosen provider/model/prompt/schema configuration under the accepted readiness thresholds.
acceptance: Each of three full runs achieves at least 48/50 case outcomes with zero critical errors of project, amount, date, commitment or source basis. Required clarification is correct; avoidable clarification on clear evidence lowers quality.

Report STT, image extraction, retrieval and final persisted effects separately. Check prohibited mutations, omitted segments, stale corrections, tenant leakage and incomplete-source handling, not just response text.

Prove the application-owned route order, image capability restriction, unsupported schema/tool responses, stalls and provider failures. User UI has no model selector. Record actual routes and metered costs.

Measure ordinary-source 95% within 60 seconds from full durable acceptance; long audio is measured separately without imposing a duration cap. Preserve useful slower routes according to the accepted throughput policy.
Version inputs and independent expectations. Attach all failures/remediation and candidate evidence; no averaging across runs to conceal a failing run or critical case.
tests: Three actual end-to-end corpus executions and separate component diagnostics for failures.
Forced fallback/error/timeout and missing-segment scenarios on the application integration.
Retrieval deletion/revision/cutover, similar aliases, relative dates, unknown tax and approximate/agreed money.
nonGoals: No fabricated benchmark from provider catalog speeds or substitution for four-week live-alpha metrics.
integration: Consumes E1 independent corpus and J2 assembled app; I2 supplies safe metrics. Reports return concrete repairs to owning feature issues and updates the P07 evidence register.

entries.title: [J4] Qualify devices, push and Calendar over the required interval
entries.problem: Browser emulation and local state machines cannot certify phone recording, actual push delivery or persistent Google authorization.
entries.solution: Qualify the integrated candidate on the required physical devices and two real Google accounts, with recorded versions and the accepted observation interval. Exercise current permissions, notification rules, Calendar reconciliation and safe client updates.
acceptance: Record actual tester phones plus physical iPhone/Android coverage, browser and installed PWA modes, and desktop Chrome/Edge/Safari. Unknown/untested versions remain unqualified.

Prove long recording, interruption, storage pressure, draft recovery, upload resume, media readability, playback and current access denial. Distinguish best-effort browser recovery from full offline or background guarantees.

Use two bosses/devices for source read synchronization, mute/snooze/quiet-time, changed deadline/recipient before send, permission withdrawal and old-push navigation to current data. A sent push is not a read receipt.

Use two Google accounts for date-only/DST/5-minute markers, task/event copies, personal hide/move, reconnect, unknown writes and duplicate suppression. Record operation beyond one week and measure the independent 95%/60-second sync target.
Exercise actual compatible release/PWA update while recording/uploading and validate session/account revocation without restoring old authority.
tests: Versioned physical-device procedure with screenshots/redacted traces and actual outcomes.
Calendar lifecycle after the required elapsed interval plus concurrent changes and lost response/change signals.
Push and release failure matrix across both users and devices, with current permission checks.
nonGoals: No emulator-only pass, accelerated-clock substitute for credential lifetime, automatic alpha activation or final styling.
integration: J2 supplies joined core, F/G supply actual integrations and I7 release/update. Findings return to owning modules; J5 consumes these device/external proofs.

Own external-consumer composition for MembershipRevoked: F3 delivery denial/device cleanup and G1/G3 transfer stop/managed-copy cleanup. Together with J2 core consumers, prove the entire revocation flow while uploads, tasks and external calls are active.

entries.title: [J5] Qualify complete core and hand off to UX integration and alpha rehearsal
entries.problem: Completed feature issues do not yet establish a complete, recoverable core or give designers and the alpha operator a truthful handoff.
entries.solution: Join all core and operational evidence on an identified integrated candidate. Exercise complete barebones paths, recovery, export/delete, authorization, telemetry and release behavior; publish a core delivery dossier for subsequent UX integration and alpha rehearsal.
acceptance: Every accepted core feature maps to an integrated operation, reachable barebones control where relevant, owner and proof. All applicable P01–P12 cases have real results and links; no accepted requirement disappears as not applicable.

Re-run impacted integration tests after final merges. Confirm consistent tenant snapshot export, deletion invalidation/purge, complete backups and measured RPO/RTO quarantine restore on the selected plans.
Verify critical failure paths and actual owner alerts with redacted logs. Record all-in costs, free-plan constraints and the current supported-device matrix.

Hand UX agents a stable operation/state catalogue, runnable core instructions and exact outstanding presentation integration. Hand the alpha operator the readiness register, rehearsal/onboarding procedures and four-week assessment instructions.

Core qualification is not live alpha or final UI acceptance. Any outstanding design integration or required evidence remains explicitly pending; do not claim readiness merely because the issue series is nearing completion.
tests: Full integrated regression through real modules plus independent recovery/export/deletion/access probes.
Evidence audit maps each accepted contract and P01–P12 case to current-revision output.
Operator reproduction from clean setup and fault-triggered alert inspection without secrets.
nonGoals: No final visual-design implementation, production activation without its scope, or automatic four-week alpha success.
integration: Own the last cross-module join including I3/I4/I6/I7 UI/commands, Calendar and push alongside the core. If a missing seam prevents proof, add/resolve its concrete prerequisite instead of waiving the requirement.
